thread:
alex: FYI p99 for /v1/generate jumped ~400ms after the routing policy flip. p50/p95 look stable. dashboard shows a big transport vs processing split. anyone else seeing this? :eyes:
maria: I see it too. transport_time seems to be the bulk for the tail on canary traffic. low payloads mostly. could be client-side queueing or a transport regression.
alex: here's the console filter I used: `route=/v1/generate AND variant=canary` then split by 'transport_ms' vs 'server_ms' — transport dominates at p99.
jamal: @alex quick reminder: console aggregates transport+server differently depending on how the exporter tags samples. if the agent tags transport separately we might be double counting in some rollups. worth validating ingestion tags.
kai: can we diff router logs vs worker start times? run `rg "enqueue_time|worker_start" -n logs/2024-*/router | sed -n '1,80p'` and compare with traces.
console-bot: ALERT: telemetry alert fired - /v1/generate p99 > 350ms (region: eu-west-1) - triggered 1790123460
sre-jen: also check retries inclusion. dashboard has a toggle, but the sampled rollups sometimes include retry hops which inflate tail. try `include_retries=false` for a quick sanity check.
maria: quick trace sample i looked at shows client TCP handshake spikes from a single IP range and then a normal server processing time. feels networky rather than server.
alex: good catch. i'll slice by client_ip_subnet and re-run the pctl query. if it's network, rolling back routing weight won't help. if it's server queueing, we need to revisit burst capacity config.
jamal: also confirm the console's percentiles are coming from tdigest vs raw-sample rollup — mixing sources can cause odd p99 behavior after routing weight shifts.
kai: grabbing router+gateway traces now. will paste a short diff in this thread shortly.
alex: thanks, team. next steps: (1) kai to paste short router vs worker diff; (2) i'll toggle include_retries and slice by client subnet; (3) ops to verify canary hosts' NIC errors. report back in ~30m. :thumbsup:
